references.text: Joshua sent two spies out from Shittim to explore the land, especially Jericho. They came to the house of the prostitute Rahab.
The spies gave Rahab an oath that they would show her mercy when the Lord gave them the land.
The spies gave Rahab instructions and swore an oath to spare her and her family.
Joshua commanded that the city be devoted to destruction, but that the prostitute Rahab and all who were in her house should live, because she had hidden the spies.
Rahab and her family were spared, and she continued to live among Israel because she had hidden the sent spies.
The book of Hebrews mentions Rahab's faith, which led to her not perishing with the disobedient, because she received the spies in peace.
James refers to Rahab as an example of justification by works, since she welcomed the messengers and sent them out by another route.
